steps.body:
f′ is a function. So differentiate it again.

**f″** is the derivative of the derivative — the rate at which the SLOPE is changing. If f is position and f′ is velocity, then f″ is acceleration.

A car can be moving forward (f′ > 0) while slowing down (f″ < 0). Direction and change-of-direction are different questions.

explanationVariants: f′(x) = 3x² − 12x, and differentiating again gives f″(x) = 6x − 12. At x = 1 that is −6.
Each differentiation is an independent application of the power rule.

commonErrors.feedback: That is f′(1) = 3 − 12 = −9, the first derivative. Differentiate once more: f″ = 6x − 12.
That is the coefficient of x in f″ = 6x − 12; you still have to substitute x = 1 and subtract 12.
That is the constant term of f″. At x = 1 the 6x contributes 6, giving 6 − 12 = −6.

widget.prompt: Trace f(x) = x³ until the tangent slope reads 12. Then ask what the slope of the SLOPE is doing.
widget.successFeedback: Slope 12 at x = 2, since f′(x) = 3x². The first derivative is how fast f changes; the second is how fast THAT changes — position, velocity, acceleration are the same three questions asked of one curve.
widget.lowFeedback: The tangent is still shallower than 12.
widget.highFeedback: The tangent has passed a slope of 12.

explanationVariants: Positive velocity means moving forward; negative acceleration means the velocity is falling. So the car is moving forward and slowing down.
The sign of f′ is direction; the sign of f″ is whether that speed is growing or shrinking.

widget.prompt: At time t, a car has f′(t) = 20 and f″(t) = −4. What is it doing?

options.label: Moving forward, and slowing down.
options.feedback: Right — positive velocity, negative acceleration. Braking while still going forward.

options.label: Reversing.
options.feedback: Reversing needs f′ < 0. The velocity is +20: firmly forward.

options.label: Moving forward and speeding up.
options.feedback: Speeding up needs f″ > 0. Here the acceleration is negative, so the velocity is falling.

options.label: Stopped.
options.feedback: Stopped means f′ = 0. The car is doing 20.

steps.body:
The second derivative also has a shape meaning:

**f″ > 0** → the slope is increasing → the curve bends **upward** (concave up, holding water).
**f″ < 0** → the curve bends **downward**.

That is how a critical point gets convicted: flat *and* bending upward is a valley.

explanationVariants: f′(x) = 2x is zero at x = 0, and f″(x) = 2 > 0, so the curve bends upward there: a minimum.
Flat plus concave up is a valley. Flat plus concave down is a peak. Flat plus f″ = 0 is undecided.

widget.prompt: f(x) = x² has f′(0) = 0 and f″(0) = 2. What is at x = 0?

options.label: A minimum — flat, and bending upward.
options.feedback: Right. The second derivative is what promotes a critical point from suspect to verdict.

options.label: A maximum.
options.feedback: A maximum needs the curve to bend DOWNWARD, f″ < 0. Here f″ = 2, firmly positive.

options.label: A flat pause, like x³ at 0.
options.feedback: x³ has f″(0) = 0 — undecided. Here f″ = 2, which settles it: the curve turns upward.

options.label: Cannot tell without more information.
options.feedback: You have everything: f′ = 0 says flat, f″ > 0 says bending upward. That is a minimum.

hints: Differentiate three times, one step at a time. Do not try to shortcut it.
One more: f‴ = 24x + 12. Now put x = 1.
explanationVariants: f′ = 4x³ + 6x²; f″ = 12x² + 12x; f‴ = 24x + 12. At x = 1 that is 36.
Each derivative is a fresh function; there is no shortcut past differentiating one at a time.

widget.prompt: f(x) = x⁴ + 2x³. Find f‴(1) (the third derivative at 1).

commonErrors.feedback: That is only the 24x term. The constant 12 from differentiating 12x is still there: 24 + 12 = 36.
That is f′(1) = 4 + 6. Two more differentiations to go.
That is f″(1) = 12 + 12 = 24, or a slip. Take one more derivative: f‴ = 24x + 12 → 36.

takeaways: f″ is the rate at which the slope changes: position → velocity → acceleration.
f′ > 0 with f″ < 0 is moving forward while slowing down. Direction and change-of-direction are different questions.
f″ > 0 means the curve bends upward, which is how a flat point is convicted as a minimum.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: what the derivative of a PRODUCT really is.

concept.body: Do it in two separate passes. First differentiate f to get f′ — and then treat f′ as a brand-new function and differentiate THAT. There is no shortcut; there are just two applications of the same rules.

explanationVariants: Differentiate twice, substituting only at the very end.

commonErrors.feedback: That is f″'s coefficient, or f′(1). Substitute x = 2 into f″ = 12x: 24.
That is f′(2) = 6(4) = 24 doubled, or a slip. f′ = 6x², f″ = 12x, f″(2) = 24.
